what_its_for: Desloratadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It works by blocking histamine, the natural substance your body releases during an allergic reaction.
how_to_take: Take desloratadine by mouth, with or without food. If you are using the dissolving tablet (orally disintegrating tablet), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve completely before swallowing — do not chew it. If you are using the liquid syrup, measure your dose carefully using the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the medicine. Do not use a regular household spoon as it may give you the wrong amount.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 5 mg (one tablet or one teaspoon of syrup) once daily. Children 6 to 11 years: The usual dose is 2.5 mg (half a tablet or half a teaspoon of syrup) once daily. Children 1 to 5 years: The usual dose is 1.25 mg once daily. Children 6 to 11 months: The usual dose is 1 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions, as doses may be adjusted for kidney or liver problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store desloratadine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Desloratadine generally does not cause drowsiness in most people, but some individuals may feel sleepy. If this happens to you, avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication as it may increase any drowsiness. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you are taking, as some may interact with desloratadine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: a severe allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or a severe skin rash; fast or irregular heartbeat; seizures; or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also call your doctor if your allergy symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment, or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Desloratadine starts working within 1 hour of taking your first dose. Most people notice full relief of their allergy symptoms within a few hours. It is a long-acting medication, so you only need to take it once a day to keep your symptoms under control.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older patients may be more sensitive to the effects of the medication. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Breastfeeding: Desloratadine may pass into breast milk. Consult your doctor before taking this medication while breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or have you take the medication less often. Always tell your doctor about any kidney or liver problems before starting this medication.
